items.gloss_md: State in the south-west; capital Stuttgart.

attrs.mnemonic: (de) Baden-Württemberg: Hauptstadt Stuttgart – "Stutengarten", deshalb das Pferd im Stadtwappen (und im Porsche-Logo).
attrs.anecdote: The state's long-running advertising slogan, since 1999, is "Wir können alles. Außer Hochdeutsch." It was formed in 1952 by merging three post-war states, after a referendum.

items.gloss_md: Largest state, in the south-east; capital München.

attrs.mnemonic: (de) Bayern ist das größte Land und ein Freistaat – wie Sachsen und Thüringen.
attrs.anecdote: In 1949 the Bavarian Landtag was the only state parliament to reject the Grundgesetz, while still accepting it as binding if two thirds of the states ratified it.

items.gloss_md: Capital of Germany, a city-state surrounded by Brandenburg.

attrs.mnemonic: Berlin is an island in Brandenburg – city and state at the same time.
attrs.anecdote: John F. Kennedy's "Ich bin ein Berliner" (1963) and mayor Klaus Wowereit's "arm, aber sexy" (2003) are the city's most quoted lines.

items.gloss_md: State around Berlin; capital Potsdam.

attrs.mnemonic: (de) Brandenburg ist der Ring, Berlin die Füllung – wie beim Berliner (Pfannkuchen). Hauptstadt Potsdam, bekannt durch die Potsdamer Konferenz 1945.
attrs.anecdote: Potsdam is home to Sanssouci, the summer palace of Frederick the Great, who asked to be buried there next to his dogs; his wish was fulfilled only in 1991.

items.gloss_md: Smallest state: the cities Bremen and Bremerhaven in the north-west.

attrs.mnemonic: (de) Zwei Städte, ein Land: Bremen und Bremerhaven, rund 60 km auseinander. Kennzeichen HB = Hansestadt Bremen.
attrs.anecdote: In the Grimm tale the Town Musicians of Bremen (donkey, dog, cat, rooster) never actually reach Bremen – they settle in the robbers' house on the way. The city honours them anyway with a statue next to the town hall, which, with the Roland, is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

items.gloss_md: City-state and port on the Elbe in the north.

attrs.mnemonic: (de) Kennzeichen HH = Hansestadt Hamburg, offiziell "Freie und Hansestadt Hamburg".
attrs.anecdote: Hamburg has around 2,500 bridges, more than Venice and Amsterdam combined; and the Beatles honed their act in its St. Pauli clubs in 1960–62.

items.gloss_md: State in the centre-west; capital Wiesbaden, largest city Frankfurt.

attrs.mnemonic: (de) Hessen: Hauptstadt Wiesbaden, nicht das größere Frankfurt – eins von vier Ländern, deren Hauptstadt nicht die größte Stadt ist (mit NRW, Sachsen, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern).
attrs.anecdote: Hessen's 1946 constitution still allowed the death penalty until a 2018 referendum removed it, although the Grundgesetz had abolished it in 1949.

items.gloss_md: State on the Baltic coast in the north-east; capital Schwerin.

attrs.mnemonic: (de) Hauptstadt Schwerin, nicht das größere Rostock – das Schloss steht im Schweriner See.
attrs.anecdote: It is the most thinly populated German state; the chalk cliffs on its island Rügen were painted by Caspar David Friedrich ("Kreidefelsen auf Rügen", 1818).

items.gloss_md: Large state in the north-west; capital Hannover.

attrs.mnemonic: (de) Niedersachsen grenzt gar nicht an Sachsen: Die alten Sachsen lebten im Nordwesten, der Name wanderte erst später mit dem Herzogstitel nach Osten. Wappen: das Sachsenross.
attrs.anecdote: Through the "VW law" the state of Niedersachsen holds a 20 % voting stake in Volkswagen, whose headquarters is in Wolfsburg.

items.gloss_md: Most populous state, in the west; capital Düsseldorf.

attrs.mnemonic: (de) Hauptstadt Düsseldorf, nicht das größere Köln – die beiden pflegen ihre Rivalität bis zum Bier (Alt gegen Kölsch).
attrs.anecdote: It was created in 1946 by the British occupation authorities by merging the northern Rhineland with Westphalia ("Operation Marriage"); Lippe joined in 1947.

items.gloss_md: State in the west on the Rhine and Mosel; capital Mainz.

attrs.mnemonic: (de) Rheinland + Pfalz: 1946 von der französischen Besatzungsmacht aus Teilen zusammengesetzt. Hauptstadt Mainz – Stadt Gutenbergs.
attrs.anecdote: Johannes Gutenberg developed printing with movable metal type in Mainz around 1450; the city's university bears his name.

items.gloss_md: Small state on the French border; capital Saarbrücken.

attrs.mnemonic: (de) "So groß wie das Saarland" – das kleinste Flächenland dient Journalisten als Flächeneinheit (ca. 2.570 km²).
attrs.anecdote: Saarland joined the Federal Republic only on 1 January 1957, after its voters rejected a European statute for the Saar in a 1955 referendum.

items.gloss_md: State in the east; capital Dresden.

attrs.mnemonic: (de) Hauptstadt Dresden, aber Leipzig ist größer. Sachsen ist wie Bayern und Thüringen ein Freistaat.
attrs.anecdote: Dresden's nickname is "Elbflorenz" (Florence on the Elbe); its Frauenkirche, destroyed in 1945, was rebuilt and reconsecrated in 2005.

items.gloss_md: State in the centre-east; capital Magdeburg.

attrs.mnemonic: (de) Magdeburg – denk an die Magdeburger Halbkugeln: Magdeburgs Bürgermeister Otto von Guericke ließ 1654 (vor dem Reichstag in Regensburg) Pferdegespanne vergeblich an zwei luftleer gepumpten Halbkugeln ziehen.
attrs.anecdote: Its advertising slogan was "Wir stehen früher auf"; Martin Luther published his 95 Theses in 1517 in Wittenberg, which lies in Sachsen-Anhalt.

items.gloss_md: Northernmost state, between North Sea and Baltic; capital Kiel.

attrs.mnemonic: (de) Das Land zwischen den Meeren: Nordsee und Ostsee. Hauptstadt Kiel an der Kieler Förde.
attrs.anecdote: The Kieler Woche held each June is one of the largest sailing events in the world.

items.gloss_md: State in the centre; capital Erfurt.

attrs.mnemonic: (de) Thüringen = "grünes Herz Deutschlands", mittendrin; Hauptstadt Erfurt.
attrs.anecdote: The Weimar Republic took its name from the Thuringian town of Weimar, where the national assembly met in 1919 – the town of Goethe and Schiller.

items.gloss_md: Capital of Bayern, on the Isar.

attrs.mnemonic: (de) München = "bei den Mönchen" – daher das Münchner Kindl, ein Mönch, im Stadtwappen.
attrs.anecdote: The Oktoberfest began in 1810 as the wedding celebration of Crown Prince Ludwig and Princess Therese; the festival ground is still called the Theresienwiese.

items.gloss_md: Largest city of Nordrhein-Westfalen, on the Rhine.

attrs.anecdote: Construction of Cologne Cathedral started in 1248 and was completed only in 1880, more than 600 years later; "Eau de Cologne" is named after the city.

items.gloss_md: Financial centre of Germany, in Hessen.

attrs.mnemonic: (de) "Mainhattan": Hochhäuser am Main, Sitz der Europäischen Zentralbank und der Börse.
attrs.anecdote: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe was born in Frankfurt in 1749; his birthplace is now a museum.

items.gloss_md: Capital of Baden-Württemberg.

attrs.mnemonic: (de) Stuttgart = "Stutengarten" (Gestüt) – daher das Pferd im Stadtwappen, das auch im Porsche-Logo steht.
attrs.anecdote: Both Daimler and Porsche are headquartered here; Gottlieb Daimler built his first engines in a garden house in nearby Cannstatt in the 1880s.

items.gloss_md: Largest city of Sachsen.

attrs.mnemonic: (de) Leipzig ist größer als die Landeshauptstadt Dresden.
attrs.anecdote: Its Monday demonstrations in autumn 1989 ("Wir sind das Volk") helped bring down the GDR; Johann Sebastian Bach worked there as Thomaskantor from 1723 until his death.

items.gloss_md: Capital of Sachsen, on the Elbe.

attrs.mnemonic: (de) "Elbflorenz": barocke Pracht an der Elbe.
attrs.anecdote: The Dresden Elbe Valley lost its UNESCO World Heritage status in 2009 because of the Waldschlösschenbrücke – only the second site ever to be delisted.

items.gloss_md: Capital of Niedersachsen.

attrs.anecdote: From 1714 to 1837 the Electors (later Kings) of Hanover were also Kings of Great Britain, starting with George I.

items.gloss_md: Second city of Bayern, in Franconia.

attrs.anecdote: Famous for Lebkuchen and the Christkindlesmarkt; after the war the Nuremberg trials (1945–46) of the leading Nazis were held in its Palace of Justice.

items.gloss_md: Largest city of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, on the Baltic.

attrs.anecdote: A Hanseatic city whose university, founded in 1419, is one of the oldest in northern Europe.

items.gloss_md: City in northern Hessen.

attrs.anecdote: Home of the documenta, held every five years since 1955; the Brothers Grimm collected many of their fairy tales while living in Kassel.
